prompt:
Perform an independent novelty review of the two candidate hypotheses below under the EXACT NOVELTY VERDICT LIMITS block included. Do not write files, implement, run experiments, or ask the user. Search 2024–2026 robotics literature (including 2026 through Sep) using primary sources and provide exact paper/venue/URLs for direct or close priors; distinguish scientific mechanism from loss transplant. Review each separately in required structured format and recommend PROCEED / PROCEED WITH CAUTION / ABANDON. Be calibrated and permissive; ABANDON only if a named published paper already contains the result.

Candidate A: Surprise-triggered recurrent-memory reset for state-only BC-RNN. At rollout, predict next proprioceptive/object state from current state/action, normalize one-step state innovation using offline calibration; when unexpected physical outcome exceeds threshold, reset recurrent hidden state before next action, discarding stale pre-event action history. Hypothesis: after a slip/contact disturbance, hidden state summarizes a trajectory that did not occur and biases correction; invalidating it at actual transition surprise improves recovery. Closest known prior: Gated Memory Policy (GMP), arXiv:2604.18933 (2026), learns an observation-conditioned binary gate for accessing cached history, trained from offline action-prediction-error benefit, evaluates RoboMimic and a mid-task cup rotation; MEMBOT arXiv:2509.11225 uses recurrent memory under intermittent observation; Contractive Dynamical Imitation Policies (ICLR 2025) improve OOS recovery by contractive architecture; FIT (2025) uses event/future-state predictions. Delta asserted: state-transition innovation triggers destructive hidden-state invalidation after outcome mismatch, rather than learned observation-conditioned read/no-read based on whether history improves action prediction.

Candidate B: Censoring-aware bounded-action BC. Standard Gaussian BC treats logged action at +/-1 as exact command. If data are post-controller clipping, labels are censored: optimize ordinary Gaussian likelihood for interior dims and one-sided tail probability likelihood for saturated dims, still execute clipped actions. Hypothesis: inference of latent intended magnitude from boundary-censored demos reduces inward bias near action limits and improves closed-loop reach/contact success. Closest known prior: Truncated Gaussian Policy (AAAI 2025) corrects PPO policy sampling/action-boundary bias; continuous imitation error/compounding analysis in COLT 2025, but no known censored-label BC. Critical condition: establish source logger stores controller-clipped labels and enough saturation mass; absent either, kill hypothesis. Risk: may be a mere likelihood/loss swap or labels may represent real intended max commands.

Other screened priors: S2I ICRA 2025; SCIZOR ICRA 2026; DataMIL ICLR 2026; LIBERO-CF/VIFO/Safety; WorldEval/WorldGym/IRASim/WorldEcho; GPC/Q-Planning/ISR/SDP/MTIL/Mamba Policy/conformal safety/ConformalDAgger/robust offline imitation (explicitly excluded); stage/progress work FIT, SPARS, SARM, balanced behavior cloning (Autonomous Robots 2026); DARP arXiv:2606.09758; action chunking + augmentation ICLR 2026; SeedPolicy arXiv:2603.05117.

=== NOVELTY VERDICT LIMITS (these bound how you judge, never how widely you search) ===
Search exhaustively; judge calibrated. Two failures waste months equally:
passing an idea a published paper already contains, and killing a viable idea
because the territory has neighbors.
1. Proximity is information, not a verdict. Someone working nearby goes in the
   report; it is not by itself a reason to reject.
2. ABANDON has exactly one qualification: a specific published paper already
   contains this result — name that paper. No named paper, no ABANDON.
3. Crowded-but-deltaed is PROCEED: state the delta in one sentence a reviewer
   could verify. Thin or contested delta is PROCEED WITH CAUTION — say what
   would make it carry, not why it should die. CAUTION is not a safe middle:
   if you cannot name the specific thing that makes the delta thin, the
   verdict is PROCEED.
4. Concurrent or competing work is not a veto. That is a race — report it and
   let the user decide whether to run it.
5. A direct attack on a central problem is legitimate novelty when nobody has
   executed it well. "This area is hot" does not mean "this area is taken."
6. This check is an early gate, never the last one — more triage, pilots, or
   external review still stand between any idea and a paper, whatever order
   this run uses. A wrongly passed idea dies cheaply at one of them; a wrongly
   killed idea is never seen again. When torn between two verdicts, choose the
   more permissive one.
Say plainly when an idea clears the check. Do not manufacture overlap.
